statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 31 U.S.C. § 5324 — Structuring transactions to evade reporting requirements?
statutory.answer: No. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements, but the facts do not show transactions structured to avoid a CTR threshold or any intent to evade reporting.
statutory.label: contradiction
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 makes it unlawful to (i) structure or assist in structuring a transaction, (ii) for the purpose of evading the reporting requirements of 31 U.S.C. § 5313(a) (CTR reporting for currency transactions), or to cause/attempt to cause a financial institution to fail to file or to file a report with material omissions/misstatements. Here, the fact pattern shows several large cash transactions ($32,394.01; $39,893.44; $62,870.06; $69,265.66) that are each well above the typical CTR trigger amount and thus are not broken into smaller sub-$10,000 increments indicative of structuring; instead they would ordinarily be reportable as-is. The record also lacks any evidence of the required purpose/intent to evade reporting (e.g., multiple same-day deposits just under the threshold, instructions to split deposits, use of multiple branches/accounts to avoid reporting, or attempts to cause non-filing). Therefore, the conduct described does not fall within § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements.
